lessonRef.subject: ready-for-life
lessonRef.unitTitle: Job Readiness: Applications, Resumes, and Interviews
lessonRef.title: Unit performance task: understanding working-age rules locally

objective: Learners assemble their resume bullet points, application message, and reference plan into one job-readiness portfolio, and research the actual minimum working age and any permit or hour-limit rules that apply where they live, completing this unit's performance task with a factually current local check rather than an assumption.
scenario: The learner compiles the resume bullet points, application message, and reference plan from earlier this unit into a single portfolio document, then researches and records the specific minimum working age, work-permit requirement, and any hour limits that apply to their own location from a current source, since these rules genuinely vary by location.
safetyNotes: Working-age, work-permit, and hour-limit rules vary by location and change over time; the learner is asked to check a current source rather than assume a rule from somewhere else applies.
materials: resume bullet points, application message, and reference plan from earlier this unit
access to a current source on local working-age rules, or the provided reference summary
a notebook or document for the compiled portfolio

tasks.directions: Before researching, write your current guess at the minimum working age where you live.

prompts.text: Write your current guess, and whether you think there are any permit or hour-limit rules.

tasks.directions: Compile your resume bullet points, application message, and reference plan into one portfolio document.

prompts.text: My portfolio includes my resume bullet points from earlier this unit.
My portfolio includes my application message from earlier this unit.
My portfolio includes my two-person reference plan from earlier this unit.

tasks.directions: Research the actual minimum working age, permit requirement, and any hour limits that apply where you live, using a current source.

prompts.text: Record what you found: the minimum working age, whether a permit is required, and any hour limits, and name the source you checked.

tasks.directions: Compare what you found to your warm-up guess and reflect on the unit.

prompts.text: How close was your guess, and what is the one piece of this unit's portfolio you feel most confident about right now?

remediation: If a learner records a working-age rule without naming where it came from, or copies a rule from an unrelated location, reteach by requiring the source to be named explicitly and by asking the learner to state, in their own words, why a rule from a different location wouldn't necessarily apply to them.
extension: Have the learner research one additional rule relevant to a first job (such as required breaks or pay timing) for their own location and add it to the portfolio with its source.
